**Short answer:** "Active" is a property of the visit record. "Current" is the chart's working visit, which is the active visit unless a retrospective visit has been selected.

- **Active visit:** the visit for the patient that has no end date (`stopDatetime === null`). The API call uses `includeInactive=false`, so the result set is already limited to open visits. Its presence generally means the patient is in the facility.
- **Current visit:** the active visit, unless a retrospective visit has been selected. If there is no active visit and no retrospective selection, there is no current visit. If there is no active visit but a retrospective one is selected, the retrospective visit is current. `currentVisitIsRetrospective` reports which case applies.

**Documentation:** the O3 framework docs for `useVisit` state this definition (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/useVisit.md`). The JSDoc on the hook says the same thing. `VisitReturnType` marks `currentVisit` and `currentVisitIsRetrospective` as deprecated: "current visit" is not well defined outside the patient chart, so the chart should use `visitContext` instead.

**Implementation:**
- `useVisit` fetches the active visit and, when a retrospective visit UUID is stored, fetches that visit as `currentVisit`. Its effect sets the visit context to the active visit when the patient has one and no visit is manually selected. It clears the context when the current visit has just been ended.
- The patient chart keeps the working visit in `visitContext` in its global store. Chart components read `visitContext`, not the hook's `currentVisit`.
- Chart UI reflects the split. The visits widget shows "Current visit" from `visitContext`. The visit-context info label shows "Current active visit" when the visit has no stop date. Vitals uses `isActiveVisit = Boolean(visitContext && !visitContext.stopDatetime)`. The banner's "active visit" tag and the "End active visit" / "Delete active visit" menu items are tied to the active-visit concept in the e2e and test suites.

**Caveat:** the docs say the active visit is "the most recent visit without an end date". The hook code takes the first open visit in the returned results and does not sort them. I did not verify whether the server's ordering guarantees "most recent", so treat that part of the docs as unverified.

Lookups and limits: the openmrs-esm-core reads used the full repo name `github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core`, because the short name failed. I did not read `useVisitContextStore`, which stores the manually selected visit.
